met_analysis:
The Low-Pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood persisted over same region at 1730 Hrs IST of today, 24th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level tilting south-westwards with height.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Jaisalmer, centre of low-pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood, Kota, Guna, Sidhi, Daltonganj & thence southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northern parts of Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining Bangladesh now lies over South West Bengal & adjoining Bangladesh and extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level. Under its influence a low pressure area likely to form over the same region during next 24 hours.
The trough now runs from cyclonic circulation associated with the Low-Pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood to Jammu division across West Rajasthan, Punjab between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists.
The offshore trough at the mean sea level from Gujarat to Karnataka coast persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
